3.2.3 Socio-Economic Considerations
The main economic impacts of operation of the project on the local area would be from the tax revenues it would generate. Oconee County offers a 5-year tax abatement to new industry during which time only the school tax is charged. The school tax rate is currently 98 mills based on a 3.5 percent assessed valuation. The Bad Creek Project, therefore, would provide the county with approximately $950,000 annually during the first years of operation. Thereafter the full tax rate of 139 mills would be in effect, with about $1,350,000 accruing to the county annually. This represents about 25 percent of real and personal property taxes collected in Oconee County in 1974. Oconee County has undergone a reassessment program, with the possibility that the tax rate could have been changed.
Little or no increases in local government operating expenses are expected to occur as a result of the operation of this project. The Applicant states that only 12 full-time employees would be required for the operation of the project. This should have little impact on the local economy.
Development of the proposed hiking trail and related features should have minimal socio-economic impacts on the local area. The development could be beneficial in that primitive hiking recreational opportunities would be made available to the local population.
3.2.4 Air Quality and Noise
After construction, the Project would have no adverse effect on the atmosphere. Due to the remote location of the project works and the underground location of the powerhouse, noise from project operation would be minimal. A minor amount of noise would be created by the transformers and transmission line. The projected transformer and transmission line noise, based on project specifications and experience with similar equipment at other sites, would be about 80 dBA at the site boundary closest to the transformers and less than the ambient noise level of 70 dBA close to the Lower Whitewater Falls.
